### Graphs {.unnumbered}

We define graph $\mathscr{G}(\mathscr{N}, \sim)$ as an ordered pair whose first entry is a set $\mathscr{N}$ containing nodes, and second entry a relation $\sim$ which indicates edges between nodes ($i \sim j$ means "$i$ is connected to $j$ in $\mathscr{G}$", for instance). There are $n = |\mathscr{N}|$ nodes, which each represent individuals in the study sample. We further define $\mathscr{N_i} = \{j \in \mathscr{N}: i \sim j\}$ as the "network exposure units" for person $i$. The  set contains the names of all the nodes $i$ is connected to. Define $\mathbf{X}_{\mathscr{N_i}}$ as the sub-vector of $\mathbf{X}$ which contains entries related to person $i$'s network exposure units.
